question: What will receiving financial advice in the future look like for clients?

claims.text: Position: AI-enabled experiences and new paid offers. On the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said the firm is working with a leading AI agent firm on a build-out and can now meet clients' trust needs with an AI-powered capability from wealth.com, with tax to follow. He said that over time these efforts will create opportunities for enhanced experiences and new fee-based offers. He also said that, according to research, more than half of Schwab's clients are willing to pay for AI financial tools, and that every sales, service and advice professional uses AI every day in client interactions.

Position: more holistic, bespoke advice, backed by technology. On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Raymond James CEO Paul Shoukry said the firm spent $1.1 billion on technology and AI, covering adviser tools and client tools. He said advisers have been expected, and will continue to be expected, to provide more holistic and bespoke financial advice over time. He said this requires the firm to provide technology and that AI can help. He also named lending (SBL and mortgage) and insurance among the capabilities needed.

Position: planning built around the whole financial picture. In its June 2025 investor day deck, Raymond James describes providing client, market and planning insights to create plans supporting a client's full financial situation, plus the tools, products and services to execute them.

Position: more service models and client segments. Edward Jones's 2025 10-K (published March 2026) describes substantial investments in initiatives to meet clients' planning, investing, saving, spending, borrowing and comprehensive needs. The initiatives include Financial Planning Services, where clients get a more personalized experience with additional planning capabilities. They also include High Net Worth (expanded advice, planning, products and services across multiple service models), Workplace, and a new digital platform for Next Generation investors. The filing says the firm cannot reliably predict the timing or outcome of these initiatives.

Position: the workplace as a route into advice relationships. On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Morgan Stanley CFO Sharon Yeshaya said that for people who do not yet have an advice-based relationship, the firm is working on a referral model. She said it can begin as early as financial education and with new 401(k) assets, helping people better understand where they could use advice.

Position: advisors asked to do more, with alternatives and AI in the mix (trade press, indicative only). An October 2026 Morgan Stanley-tagged trade article cites a September 2026 Fidelity survey of 1,311 plan sponsors, in which 93% work with an advisor. The article concludes that advisors are being asked to do more and that clients will reward those who deliver on the expanded role. A separate InvestmentNews piece (14 October 2026) says Merrill Lynch, Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo continue to boost sales of alternative investments and AI functions for financial advisors in 2026.

adjacent.text: Vanguard research (published June 2025), based on a survey of 12,443 investors including 7,746 advised clients, found that 86% of advised clients report greater peace of mind and 76% say advice saves them time. At sign-up, 87% considered portfolio value, 74% emotional value, 69% financial value and 38% time value.
adjacent.differs_because: This describes what advised clients value today, not a forecast of how advice will be delivered in future.

adjacent.text: A November 2026 trade article on an advisor who left Edward Jones for LPL describes a practice model rooted in listening before advising and in connecting investments, retirement, business interests, charitable giving and legacy.
adjacent.differs_because: This is trade-press reporting on one advisor's practice at an independent firm. It is indicative only and is not a firm or industry view of the future.

gaps.what: No independent research or forecast in the evidence describes the future client advice experience across the industry. The claims above are firm statements of intent or initiatives, not outcomes.
gaps.suggested_source: Industry research on future advice delivery (e.g., consultancy or investor-survey studies) and firm investor-day presentations

gaps.what: The evidence has little on client-side preferences about AI or digital advice, apart from Schwab's cited research on willingness to pay. Merrill and Bank of America evidence on future client experience is not found.
gaps.suggested_source: Merrill / Bank of America GWIM earnings calls and client surveys
